mainTopic: The אבות and תולדות of damage by an ox: קרן, its sub-types, and the sources for שן and רגל
overview: The גמרא finishes its example from טומאה, where the תולדות are weaker than their אבות, and asks how it works in damages. רב פפא answers that in damages some תולדות are like their אבות and some are not. A ברייתא lists the three אבות of an ox: קרן, שן and רגל. The גמרא proves from two פסוקים that 'goring' means using a horn, and explains that the second פסוק shows the difference between תם and מועד applies to an attached horn too. It then lists the תולדות of קרן: pushing, biting, crouching and kicking. Along the way it learns from the words יגח and יגף that an ox מועד for people is מועד for animals, but not the other way around. Since the תולדות of קרן are fully like קרן, רב פפא must have meant שן and רגל. The גמרא begins bringing the פסוקים for רגל and שן, and the second proof continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: In טומאה the offshoots are weaker than the primary sources
steps.stepSummary: The list of אבות הטומאה ends with טמא מת. The גמרא shows that here the תולדות are not like the אבות: an אב makes people and vessels impure, but a תולדה only makes food and drink impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who is impure from a dead body. Their offshoots are not like them. A primary source of impurity makes people and vessels impure. The offshoots only make food and drink impure; they do not make people or vessels impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its list of אבות הטומאה. It shows that in this area of law, the 'children' (תולדות) are weaker than the 'parents' (אבות).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא asked whether a תולדה always has the same law as its אב. In שבת they are the same, but טומאה is a clear case where they differ: the תולדה has a lower level of impurity. This sets up two possible models before the גמרא turns to damages.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who became impure from contact with a dead body
A primary source or main category (here, of impurity)
Offshoots or subcategories that come from an אב
Like them, having the same law

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a תולדה of טומאה is not impure at all. It is impure, just at a lower level, so it can only make food and drink impure.

phrases.english: and one who is impure from a dead body.
Their offshoots are not like them;
for a primary source makes a person and vessels impure,
while offshoots make food and drink impure,
but do not make a person and vessels impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the טומאה example, the counterpart to שבת, from just before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In טומאה, תולדות are weaker than אבות: they make only food and drink impure, not people or vessels.

steps.title: What about damages?
steps.stepSummary: Having seen one area where offshoots match their sources (שבת) and one where they do not (טומאה), the גמרא asks which model fits damages.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, in damages, what is the rule?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks its real question. This line sets up the next step, where רב פפא gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה used the words אבות נזיקין, which suggests there are also תולדות. The גמרא wants to know whether those תולדות carry the same law as their אבות, as in שבת, or a different law, as in טומאה.

phrases.english: Here, what?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means in the laws of damages that our משנה is teaching.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the שבת/טומאה comparison to damages
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the תולדות of damages have the same law as their אבות

steps.title: רב פפא: some are like their sources, some are not
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that in damages it is mixed: some תולדות have the same law as their אב and some do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Some of them are like their sources, and some of them are not like their sources.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that damages does not follow just one model. Some offshoots match their source and some do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mixed answer forces the גמרא to go through each אב of damage one by one, to see which of its תולדות match it. That is why it now starts listing the אבות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answer sets the plan for the rest of the סוגיא: going through each אב to find its תולדות and check whether they share its law.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
There are some of them that are like them,
and there are some of them that are not like them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: יֵשׁ מֵהֶן כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In damages it is mixed: some תולדות are like their אבות and some are not.

steps.title: Three primary kinds of damage by an ox
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the תורה names three אבות of damage done by an ox: קרן (horn), שן (tooth) and רגל (foot).
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Three primary kinds of damage were said about an ox: the horn, the tooth and the foot.
steps.whatsHappening: To explain רב פפא, the גמרא brings a ברייתא listing the three main ways an ox causes damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each kind of damage is named after a body part. קרן is goring, שן is eating, and רגל is trampling while walking. These are אבות because the תורה speaks about them, so the גמרא will next look for the source of each one.

keyTerms.meaning: Horn: an ox goring to do damage
Tooth: an animal eating someone's produce
Foot: an animal trampling things as it walks

steps.confusionAlert: קרן, שן and רגל are not only about those exact body parts. They are names for types of damage, each with its own pattern.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Three primary categories were stated about an ox –
the horn, and the tooth, and the foot.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת נֶאֶמְרוּ בְּשׁוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the list of אבות needed to apply רב פפא's answer
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox has three אבות of damage: קרן, שן and רגל.

steps.title: Where do we learn קרן from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source in the תורה for קרן as a category of damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we know קרן from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins with the first אב and asks for its source. This line sets up the proof that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the three אבות 'were stated' in the תורה, so each one needs a פסוק. The גמרא starts with קרן.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: Horn – from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first item on the list
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches קרן as an אב of damage

steps.title: 'If it gores' means with a horn, proven from צדקיה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא answers that the תורה's words כי יגח refer to קרן, because goring is done with a horn. The proof is from צדקיה בן כנענה, who made iron horns to 'gore' ארם.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'If it gores' — goring means only with a horn, as it says: 'And צדקיה son of כנענה made himself iron horns and said: So says ה׳, with these you will gore ארם.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for קרן. The תורה says an ox that 'gores,' and another פסוק shows that goring is done with horns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not say the word 'horn' in the law; it says 'gores.' The ברייתא links the word 'gore' to horns using a פסוק where the same verb is used for horns. So the תורה's case of goring is the category of קרן.

keyTerms.meaning: If it gores (from the תורה's law of an ox)
And so on: the rest of the פסוק

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"If it gores" –
phrases.notes: שמות 21:28

phrases.english: goring is only with a horn,
as it is said: "And Zedekiah son of Chenaanah made himself

phrases.aramaic: קַרְנֵי בַרְזֶל, וַיֹּאמֶר: כֹּה אָמַר ה׳,
phrases.english: horns of iron, and said: So says the Lord,
phrases.notes: מלכים א 22:11

phrases.english: with these you shall gore Aram, etc."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן: כִּי יִגַּח – אֵין נְגִיחָה אֶלָּא קֶרֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה's 'כי יגח' is קרן, since goring is done with a horn, as seen with צדקיה's iron horns.

steps.title: A second פסוק: horns used to gore nations
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds a second proof from משה's ברכה to יוסף, where horns are described as the tool used to gore.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it also says: 'His firstborn ox, majesty is his, and his horns are the horns of a wild ox; with them he will gore nations.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings another פסוק that ties goring to horns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'with them he will gore' refers back to the horns, so again goring is done with a horn. Why a second proof was needed is the question the גמרא asks in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: And it also says (bringing another פסוק)
A wild ox, known for strong horns

steps.whatToRemember: In damages, some תולדות match their אבות and some do not. The three אבות of an ox are קרן, שן and רגל, and קרן comes from the תורה's 'כי יגח,' since goring is done with a horn.

phrases.english: And it says: "His firstborn ox, majesty is his,
phrases.notes: דברים 33:17

phrases.english: and his horns are the horns of a wild ox,
with them he shall gore nations."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק to support the proof in step 6
steps.raayaObject: That נגיחה (goring) means damage done with a horn
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 33:17, 'his horns... with them he shall gore nations'

steps.title: Why did the ברייתא need a second verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the extra proof introduced with 'ואומר' adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the point of 'and it also says'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops and asks why the ברייתא brought a second פסוק after the first one already proved that goring is done with a horn. This question sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ואומר signals that the first proof was not fully enough. The גמרא wants to know what was missing from the צדקיה פסוק, so that the משה פסוק was needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it says': a formula that brings an extra פסוק to add to the first proof

phrases.english: What is the point of 'and it says'?
phrases.notes: This points back to the second proof in the ברייתא, the ברכה of משה to יוסף.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why step 7's added proof was needed after step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the second פסוק teaches that the first פסוק did not.

steps.title: First answer: a תורה law cannot be learned from נביאים
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the second פסוק was brought because we do not learn תורה laws from דברי קבלה, so a פסוק from the תורה itself was needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that we do not learn matters of תורה from the words of tradition, come and hear: 'His firstborn ox, majesty is his.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests an answer. The first proof came from נביאים, which may not be a valid source for a תורה law, so the ברייתא added a פסוק from the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The צדקיה פסוק is in מלכים, which counts as דברי קבלה. If a law of damages cannot be based on such a פסוק, the ברייתא needs the פסוק in דברים to back it up.

keyTerms.meaning: Laws that come from the חמשה חומשי תורה
'Words of tradition': the books of נביאים and כתובים
We do not learn or derive
'And if you will say': brings up a possible objection

phrases.english: And if you will say
matters of Torah from words of tradition
phrases.notes: Words of tradition means the books of the Prophets and Writings, like the צדקיה story.

phrases.english: we do not learn,
come and hear: 'His firstborn ox, majesty is his.'
phrases.notes: דברים 33:17

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה מִדִּבְרֵי קַבָּלָה לָא יָלְפִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a first answer to step 8's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second פסוק was needed because a law cannot be learned from נביאים.

steps.title: This is only revealing a fact, not learning a law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the first answer: the צדקיה פסוק does not teach a law. It only shows a plain fact, that goring is done with a horn.
steps.simpleTranslation: But is this a derivation of law? It is just revealing a fact, that goring is done with a horn!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the answer from step 9. The rule against learning from נביאים does not apply here, because we are only finding out what the word 'gore' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a law cannot be derived from נביאים. A פסוק in נביאים can still show us a simple fact about the world, such as what part of the body is used for goring. So the first פסוק was good enough, and the next step gives a different reason for the second one.

keyTerms.meaning: Just revealing a fact, not creating a new law

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying we can learn laws from נביאים. It is saying that showing what a word means is not 'learning a law' at all.

phrases.english: But is this a derivation?!
It is merely revealing a matter,
that goring is with a horn!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer of step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the second פסוק was needed because of the rule against learning from דברי קבלה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That rule applies only to deriving laws, not to revealing a fact like what goring means.

steps.title: Second answer: the second verse shows an attached horn has the תם and מועד difference too
steps.stepSummary: The second פסוק was needed so we would not think that the תם and מועד difference applies only to a detached horn, like צדקיה's, while an attached horn is always מועד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, you might have said: when the תורה separates a תם from a מועד, that is only with a detached horn, but with an attached horn, say it is always מועד. So come and hear: 'His firstborn ox, majesty is his.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real reason for the second פסוק. צדקיה's horns were separate pieces of iron, so the ברייתא adds a פסוק about horns attached to the animal's head.
steps.deeperAnalysis: From צדקיה alone, we might think the half-damage rule for a תם covers only an unusual case, like an ox goring with a loose horn, while goring with its own horn is normal and always pays in full. The פסוק in דברים describes horns growing on the animal ('his horns are the horns of the wild ox'). This shows that the תם and מועד difference applies to ordinary goring too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You might have said': brings up a mistaken idea that the source comes to rule out
An ox that has not gored three times; its owner pays half damages
An ox that has gored three times and its owner was warned; its owner pays full damages
Detached, meaning a horn not attached to the animal
Attached, meaning a horn growing on the animal's head

steps.whatToRemember: Both פסוקים are needed: צדקיה shows that goring means using a horn, and משה's ברכה shows that a horn attached to the animal also has the תם and מועד difference.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the usual case of קרן, an ox goring with its own horns, has the half-damage rule for a תם. This is the basic case of the אב of קרן.

phrases.english: Rather, you might have said,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי פַּלֵּיג רַחֲמָנָא בֵּין תָּם לְמוּעָד –
phrases.english: when the Merciful One distinguishes between a תם and a מועד,
that applies only to a detached horn,
phrases.notes: Like the iron horns צדקיה made, which were not part of an animal.

phrases.english: but with an attached horn,
say it is entirely מועד;
phrases.notes: Meaning the owner would always pay full damages, even the first time.

phrases.english: come and hear:
'His firstborn ox, majesty is his, etc.'
phrases.notes: The rest of the פסוק says 'his horns are the horns of a wild ox', meaning horns growing on the animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 9 with a new reason for the second פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new purpose for the second source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תם and מועד difference might apply only to a detached horn, while an attached horn would always be מועד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second פסוק shows that an attached horn also has the תם and מועד difference.

steps.title: The sub-types of goring
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists the תולדות of קרן: נגיפה, נשיכה, רביצה and בעיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are the sub-types of Horn (קרן)? Pushing, biting, crouching on things, and kicking.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes back to its list and names the 'children' (תולדות) of the damage category called קרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קרן is when an animal goes out of its way to cause harm. Any other harmful act done on purpose with its body, like pushing, biting, lying down on things or kicking, falls under the same category as a תולדה.

keyTerms.meaning: A sub-type, a 'child' of a main damage category
Horn: an animal goring or harming on purpose
Pushing with the body (in this list)
Crouching or lying down on something to damage it

steps.confusionAlert: נגיפה here means pushing with the body, a תולדה. In the next steps the word נגיפה from the פסוק turns out to mean real goring. Same word, two different uses.

phrases.english: What is a sub-type of Horn?
Pushing, biting, crouching, and kicking.
phrases.notes: Crouching means the animal lies down on things on purpose to damage them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the side discussion about the extra proof (ואומר), the ברייתא continues its list of תולדות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pushing, biting, crouching and kicking are all תולדות of קרן.

steps.title: Why is goring a main category but pushing is not?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if נגיחה is an אב because the תורה writes כי יגח, then נגיפה should also be an אב, since the תורה writes כי יגף.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes goring different, that it is called a main category? Because it is written 'if it gores.' But pushing is also written: 'if it pushes'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the list: נגיפה is written in the תורה just like נגיחה, so why is it only a תולדה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אב is something written directly in the תורה. Since the word יגף also appears in a פסוק (שמות 21:35), it seems נגיפה should count as an אב too, not just a sub-type.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? (asking why two similar things are treated differently)
A main category of damage, written in the תורה

phrases.english: What is different about goring
that we call it a main category?
Because it is written: 'if it gores.'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:28

phrases.english: Pushing is also written: 'if it pushes'!
phrases.notes: שמות 21:35

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא נְגִיחָה דְּקָרֵי לַהּ אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא's placing of נגיפה as a תולדה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's list that makes נגיפה only a תולדה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being written in the תורה is what makes something an אב, and יגף is written just like יגח.

steps.title: The pushing in the פסוק is really goring
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the נגיפה written in the פסוק is not a different act; it is the same as נגיחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This 'pushing' in the פסוק is actually goring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the word יגף in the פסוק simply means goring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the פסוק does not create a second אב. The נגיפה in the פסוק is goring with the horn, while the נגיפה in the ברייתא's list is plain pushing with the body, which is still only a תולדה.

keyTerms.meaning: This (pointing to the word in the פסוק)
It is (here: is the same as)

phrases.english: This 'pushing' is goring.
phrases.notes: He means the יגף in the פסוק, not the pushing listed in the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: יגף in the פסוק is a separate act of pushing, so it should be its own אב.
steps.terutzMaskana: יגף in the פסוק means goring, so there is only one אב here, נגיחה.

steps.title: Proof: the פסוק starts with pushing and ends with goring
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא proves that יגף means goring: the פסוק opens with נגיפה and closes with נגיחה, showing they are the same act.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: The פסוק begins with 'pushing' and ends with 'goring,' to tell you that this pushing is this goring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up its answer that יגף means goring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case in שמות 21:35–36 begins with 'if an ox יגף' and then speaks of an ox known to be a goring ox (נגח). Since it is one case described with both words, the two words must mean the same thing.

keyTerms.meaning: To tell you (to teach you a point)

phrases.english: As it is taught: It opened with 'pushing'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:35: 'if one man's ox יגף another's ox.'

phrases.english: and ended with 'goring,'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:36: 'that the ox was a goring ox in the past.'

phrases.english: to tell you:

phrases.aramaic: זוֹ הִיא נְגִיפָה זוֹ הִיא נְגִיחָה.
phrases.english: this is pushing, this is goring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 14.
steps.raayaObject: That יגף in the פסוק means goring
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading שמות 21:35–36, which starts with נגיפה and ends with נגיחה

steps.title: Then why two different words?
steps.stepSummary: If יגח and יגף mean the same thing, why does the תורה say יגח about a person and יגף about an animal?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about a person, that it is written 'if it gores,' and what is different about an animal, that it is written 'if it pushes'?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that both words mean goring, the גמרא asks why the תורה switches words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not change words for no reason. When the victim is a person it says יגח, and when the victim is an animal it says יגף, so the גמרא wants to know what the change is teaching.

phrases.english: What is different regarding a person
that it is written 'if it gores,'
and what is different regarding an animal
that it is written 'if it pushes'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא גַּבֵּי אָדָם דִּכְתִיב כִּי יִגַּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from step 15: if the words mean the same, why use both?
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the תורה uses יגח for a person and יגף for an animal

steps.title: A person can protect himself, an animal cannot
steps.stepSummary: A person has מזל, the sense to protect himself, so the תורה uses the strong word יגח. An animal lacks it, so even a light blow (יגף) can hurt it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person, who has the ability to protect himself, is described with 'if it gores.' An animal, which does not have that ability, is described with 'if it pushes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the change of words: it depends on how easily the victim gets hurt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person can defend himself, so only a strong attack (נגיחה) will injure him. An animal cannot defend itself, so even a lighter blow (נגיפה) can do serious harm. Both words describe the same act of goring; the wording matches how the damage usually happens.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: a person's ability or sense to protect himself

steps.whatToRemember: נגיפה in the פסוק is the same as נגיחה, so there is one אב, קרן. The תורה says יגח for a person, who can defend himself, and יגף for an animal, which is hurt even by a lighter blow.

phrases.english: A person, who has the ability to protect himself,
it is written 'if it gores';
an animal, which does not have that ability,
it is written 'if it pushes.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָדָם דְּאִית לֵיהּ מַזָּלָא כְּתִיב כִּי יִגַּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wording follows how easily the victim is hurt: a strong attack for a person, a lighter one for an animal.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both words mean goring. The תורה picks the word that fits the type of victim.

steps.title: A side lesson: forewarned for people means forewarned for animals
steps.stepSummary: From the different words יגח and יגף, the גמרא learns in passing that an ox that is מועד for a person is also מועד for an animal, but an ox that is מועד for an animal is not מועד for a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תורה teaches us something in passing: an ox that is forewarned for goring people is also forewarned for goring animals. But an ox that is forewarned for goring animals is not forewarned for goring people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a practical lesson that comes out of the answer it just gave about יגח and יגף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 17 said a person has מזל and can protect himself, so goring a person takes a strong blow (יגח). An animal can be hurt by a light blow (יגף). So an ox that has shown it will gore people will surely gore animals, but an ox that only gores animals has not shown it will gore people.

keyTerms.meaning: A 'forewarned' ox, one that has a record of goring, so its owner pays full damages

steps.whatToRemember: An ox that is מועד for people is מועד for animals, but an ox that is מועד for animals is not מועד for people. This comes from יגח versus יגף.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical הלכה about how much an owner pays. It grows directly out of what looked like a simple question of wording.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִלְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן –
phrases.english: And it teaches us a matter in passing:
phrases.notes: The 'it' is the תורה's choice of the two different words, יגח for a person and יגף for an animal.

phrases.english: that [an ox] forewarned regarding a person is forewarned regarding an animal,

phrases.aramaic: וּמוּעָד לִבְהֵמָה לָא הָוֵי מוּעָד לְאָדָם.
phrases.english: but [an ox] forewarned regarding an animal is not forewarned regarding a person.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִלְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a practical halacha out of the answer in step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An ox that is מועד for a person is מועד for an animal, but an ox that is מועד for an animal is not מועד for a person.

steps.title: Shouldn't biting belong under eating?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: biting is done with the teeth, so it should be a תולדה of שן, not of קרן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Biting is a תולדה of שן (damage by eating)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's decision to list biting (נשיכה) under קרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal both eats and bites with its teeth. So it seems biting should fall under שן, the category of damage by eating, rather than under קרן.

keyTerms.meaning: A sub-category of one of the main categories of damage
'Tooth': damage caused by an animal eating

phrases.english: Biting is a sub-category of Tooth!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from נגיחה and נגיפה to the next item in the ברייתא's list
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's listing of biting as a תולדה of קרן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Biting uses the teeth, just like eating, so it should belong to שן.

steps.title: Eating brings pleasure; biting does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שן involves pleasure for the animal while it damages, but biting brings it no pleasure. So biting is not like שן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. With שן, the animal gets pleasure from the damage. With this (biting), it gets no pleasure from the damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the ברייתא by pointing to a key difference between eating and biting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What defines שן is not the body part but the fact that the animal enjoys the act. Biting brings no pleasure; its only purpose is to harm. That makes it like קרן, not שן.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't sort the categories by body part. They are sorted by the nature of the act: eating brings pleasure, biting is meant only to harm.

phrases.english: No; Tooth has pleasure in its damage,
this has no pleasure in its damage.
phrases.notes: 'This' means biting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the defining feature of שן is missing from biting
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Biting uses teeth, so it belongs to שן
steps.terutzMaskana: שן is defined by the animal's pleasure; biting has none, so it belongs to קרן

steps.title: Shouldn't crouching and kicking belong under trampling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא again: crouching and kicking are done with the legs, so they should be תולדות of רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Crouching and kicking are תולדות of רגל (damage by walking)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's decision to list crouching and kicking under קרן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal crouches by bending its legs and kicks with its feet. So it seems these should fall under רגל, the category of damage done while walking.

keyTerms.meaning: Crouching or lying down on something
'Foot': damage caused by an animal as it walks

phrases.english: Crouching and kicking are a sub-category of Foot!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of challenge as step 19, now on the next items in the list
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's listing of crouching and kicking as תולדות of קרן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both use the legs, so they should belong to רגל.

steps.title: Trampling is common; crouching and kicking are not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רגל damage happens commonly, as the animal walks. Crouching on things and kicking them do not happen commonly.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. With רגל, the damage is common. With these, the damage is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the ברייתא by pointing to a key difference between trampling and crouching or kicking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: What defines רגל is that the damage is ordinary and expected, since it happens just from walking. Animals do not usually crouch on or kick things, so these are unusual acts. That makes them like קרן, not רגל.
steps.whatToRemember: The categories of damage are defined by how the damage happens, not by which body part does it. שן means pleasure, רגל means common damage, and קרן means damage that is unusual and done to harm.

phrases.english: No; Foot's damage is common,
these, their damage is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the defining feature of רגל is missing from crouching and kicking
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Crouching and kicking use the legs, so they belong to רגל
steps.terutzMaskana: רגל is defined by damage that is common; crouching and kicking are not common, so they belong to קרן

steps.title: So which category did רב פפא mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רב פפא's statement that some תולדות are not like their אבות, and asks which אב he was talking about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רב פפא said 'their תולדות are not like them,' which one was he referring to?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב פפא's statement and asks which main category he had in mind. This sets up the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא has just shown that the תולדות listed under קרן really do belong with קרן. So the open question returns: which אב did רב פפא mean when he said some תולדות are not like their אבות?

keyTerms.meaning: Their sub-categories are not like them, meaning some תולדות do not follow the same rules as their main category

phrases.english: Rather, 'their sub-categories are not like them,'
which רב פפא said, to which [category] does it refer?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא תּוֹלְדוֹתֵיהֶן לָאו כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהֶן דְּאָמַר רַב פָּפָּא אַהֵיָיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After confirming the תולדות of קרן, returns to the open question about רב פפא's statement
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which אב רב פפא meant when he said that some תולדות are not like their אבות

steps.title: Could רב פפא have meant קרן? No
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רב פפא was talking about the תולדות of קרן, then rejects this. Those תולדות have the same features as קרן: they mean to damage, they are your property, and you must guard them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say רב פפא meant these (the תולדות of קרן), that cannot be. What makes קרן special? Its intention is to damage, it is your property, and guarding it is your job. These have the same features: their intention is to damage, they are your property, and guarding them is your job!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible answer, that רב פפא meant קרן, and immediately shows that it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אב is defined by its key features. The key features of קרן are that it means to damage, it is your property, and you must guard it. Pushing, biting, crouching, and kicking, which are the תולדות of קרן, have all of these same features, so they are just like קרן and not different from it.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (it introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
What is different / what makes it special?

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that biting or kicking leave the category of קרן. It is saying the opposite: they match קרן so closely that רב פפא could not have meant them.

phrases.english: If you say he meant these,
phrases.notes: "These" means the תולדות of קרן from the ברייתא: pushing, biting, crouching, and kicking.

phrases.english: what is special about goring?
That its intention is to damage,
and it is your property, and guarding it is on you.
These too: their intention is to damage,
and they are your property, and guarding them is on you!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to step 23's question and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רב פפא was speaking about the תולדות of קרן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תולדות of קרן share every defining feature of קרן, so they cannot be called unlike their אב.

steps.title: רב פפא meant שן and רגל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that a תולדה of קרן is like קרן. רב פפא's statement was about שן and רגל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a תולדה of קרן is like קרן, and when רב פפא spoke, he was talking about שן and רגל.
steps.whatsHappening: Since קרן did not work, the גמרא gives the real answer to step 23: רב פפא meant שן and רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 showed that the תולדות of קרן share every defining feature of קרן, so they cannot be the ones that are 'not like' their אב. By elimination, רב פפא's statement must be about the תולדות of שן and רגל. Biting, crouching and kicking are not those תולדות; steps 19-22 showed that they belong under קרן.

keyTerms.meaning: A sub-category of goring is like goring

steps.whatToRemember: The תולדות of קרן are fully like קרן. רב פפא's point that some תולדות are unlike their אבות applies to שן and רגל.

phrases.english: Rather, a sub-category of goring is like goring,
and when רב פפא said it,
it was about eating and trampling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 24 with the correct one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב פפא was referring to שן and רגל, not קרן.

steps.title: Where are שן and רגל written in the תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of שן and רגל in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where are שן and רגל written?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the תורה writes about שן and רגל, and gets ready to bring a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once שן and רגל are treated as their own אבות, the גמרא wants to see them in a פסוק. The answer comes in the next steps.

phrases.english: Eating and trampling, where are they written?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 25's focus on שן and רגל by asking for their source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches the damages of שן and רגל.

steps.title: "ושלח" teaches רגל
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads "ושלח" in the פסוק as רגל, and proves it from a פסוק in ישעיהו that uses the same word for feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the ברייתא teaches: "And he sends forth" means רגל. And so it says: "that send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the word "ושלח" in the פסוק about damages refers to רגל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא proves the meaning of a word from another פסוק. In ישעיהו, "sending forth" goes with the feet of the animals, so "ושלח" here also means damage done by the feet.

keyTerms.meaning: And so it says (it brings a supporting פסוק)

phrases.english: As it was taught: "And he sends forth" — this is trampling,
phrases.notes: שמות 22:4

phrases.english: and so it says:
"that send forth the feet of the ox and the donkey."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 32:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering step 26's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רגל comes from "ושלח," proven by "משלחי רגל" in ישעיהו.

steps.title: "ובער" teaches שן
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא reads "ובער" as שן and starts bringing a supporting פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And it consumed" means שן. And so it says: "as one consumes"
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues: the next word in the פסוק, "ובער," refers to שן. Its proof פסוק continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא splits the same פסוק into two parts: "ושלח" is רגל, and "ובער" is שן. It uses the same method again and brings another פסוק where the word means eating up or consuming.

phrases.english: "And it consumed" — this is eating,
and so it says:
"as one consumes
phrases.notes: מלכים א 14:10. The quote finishes on the next עמוד.

steps.triggerLanguage: ובער זו השן וכן הוא אומר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and gives the source for שן after the source for רגל.
steps.raayaObject: That "ובער" in the פסוק refers to שן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק "כאשר יבער" in מלכים א
